body:
I DESTROYED EVIDENCE WITH BUG-1539 — the defect I identified earlier tonight — and I am reporting it rather than letting it pass as a gap nobody notices.

WHAT HAPPENED. PR-2026.json held the drain reviewer's RequestChanges at 363bd8f9f7fb with its summary and findings. I read it, then recorded my own verdict with `aida review record BUG-1441 ... --pr 2026`. The PR-keyed handshake write NEVER READS THE EXISTING FILE — that is BUG-1539, lib.rs:76429-76447, which I characterised to you at about 03:30 and then triggered myself ninety minutes later. The drain reviewer's text is gone from PR-2026.json.

IT IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM ANYWHERE ELSE. Neither PR-2026.json nor BUG-1441.json carries a `rounds` array, so STORY-1391's retention did not catch it — that path snapshots rounds on the SPEC-keyed write, and the loss was on the PR-keyed one. And `.aida/review-verdicts/` is gitignored under the deny-by-default `.aida/*` rule, so there is no commit history to restore from. I checked both before writing this.

WHAT I RECOVERED AND WHAT I DID NOT. I had printed the first ~400 characters of the summary and of finding 1 when I read the file before recording. I have put that reconstruction back into the verdict as finding F0, explicitly labelled as PARTIAL and TRUNCATED-AT-READ-TIME, attributed to "aida drain reviewer" rather than to me, and stating that I am the one who destroyed the original. Anything past 400 characters in either field is lost. I do not know how many findings the original had — I printed only the first.

TWO THINGS THIS CHANGES.

BUG-1539's SEVERITY IS HIGHER THAN I FILED IT. I described it as a clobber. It is a clobber that destroys the ONLY copy of a prior reviewer's reasoning, on a corpus with no history and no rounds on that path, triggered by the ordinary act of a second reviewer recording on the same PR. Every multi-round PR-keyed review has been losing the previous round's text all along, silently. I have no measurement of how many — the evidence of each loss is the thing that was lost.

AND PRODUCT MISATTRIBUTED THE ORIGINAL FINDING TO ME, which is downstream of the same destruction. Their mail says "YOUR FINDING, ADDRESSED THE WAY YOU RANKED SECOND" and quotes 'add TOON and JSON regression assertions ... (or normalize the state once before all renderers)'. That was the DRAIN REVIEWER's finding, not mine — recorded_by was "aida drain reviewer" — and I cannot now verify whether that exact sentence was in it, because the text I would check against is the text I deleted. I will correct the attribution to them. The irony is exact: a tool that loses the prior round makes the next seat's work look like the previous seat's.

ON #2026 ITSELF: RequestChanges stands at 9c38af7d83 on the trace-comment displacement, hold armed, and the fix is otherwise right — details in my previous mail.

I am not filing; BUG-1539 exists. If you want its description amended with this, the two facts worth adding are that the loss is unrecoverable (no rounds on that path, no git history for the directory) and that it is triggered by normal second-reviewer behaviour rather than by anything unusual.
subject: I destroyed the drain reviewer's original finding via BUG-1539 — unrecoverable, partial reconstruction restored, and the severity is higher than I filed it
